chunks: Ahmad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fazl al-Nowfaly, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man in haste, what is that which would suffice him in the optional (prayer)? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Three glorifications in the recitation, and a glorification in the bowing, and a glorification in the prostration.'
ai.seo_question: What is the abbreviated prayer procedure for someone in a hurry according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific concessions for a person performing the optional (nafl) prayer who is in a hurry, allowing them to substitute the full Quranic chapter with three glorifications (Tasbihat) during the recitation phase, one during the bowing (Ruku'), and one during the prostration (Sujood). This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding voluntary acts of worship, balancing reverence with practicality when time is constrained. It reflects the broader principle that nafl prayers, while meritorious, are not as strictly regulated as obligatory prayers, allowing for simplified forms to encourage consistent devotion.
